WHY: Every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks at runtime/compile (AbstractMethodError) and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit NPEs on null (ConcurrentHashMap forbids null), crashing startup. HOW: Provide a default e.g. `default String getShortcut() { return DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN; }` and null-validate in postInit.

WHAT: initToken unconditionally dereferences session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for unknown grantType. WHY: Token issuance that previously always succeeded with a UUID now fails with NPE (provider missing) or 500 (unregistered/custom grant string from formParams) for flows that never set a mapped GRANT_TYPE. HOW: Fall back to KeycloakModelUtils.generateId() when encoder is null or shortcut is unknown.

issues.descricao: The AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and is encoded as ':null'.
issues.textoGolden: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the constructor validates `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`). WHY: a null `rawTokenId` is silently accepted, so `encodeTokenId` produces a token id ending in `:null` and any later consumer of the raw id gets an invalid value instead of an early failure. HOW: change the argument to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

Line 73 calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — it validates grantType a second time (line 72 already does) with a message naming a different field. rawTokenId is never validated, so a null rawTokenId is accepted at construction and the advertised check/message is wrong. It should be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

The null-check message names the wrong parameter: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` validates `grantType` but reports `rawTokenId`, and it duplicates the check on line 72 while `rawTokenId` is never validated at all. The message that reaches the reader contradicts the code it guards; it should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

issues.descricao: isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut at the wrong offset (3,5 instead of 4,6) and inverts the comparison, so the event assertions never verify the token's grant type.
issues.textoGolden: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `isAccessTokenId` reads the grant shortcut from the wrong offset and inverts the comparison — `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. WHY: for the encoded id `ssttgg:raw` the grant shortcut occupies 0-based indices 4-5, so `substring(3,5)` inspects the token-type/grant boundary and can never equal the expected shortcut; combined with the inverted `return false`, the equality branch is unreachable and the matcher validates only the UUID part. As a result the new assertions in `expectCodeToToken`/`expectRefresh`/`expectDeviceCodeToToken`/`expectAuthReqIdToToken` do not actually assert the grant type and would pass even if the grant shortcut were wrong. HOW: use `items[0].substring(4, 6)` and negate the condition (`if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).

The matcher logic is inverted: line 483 returns false when the extracted grant shortcut EQUALS expectedGrantShortcut, so a token that actually carries the expected grant fails the matcher, while a token with any other grant shortcut falls through and passes. The condition should be negated: `if (!items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also note the encode site writes the grant shortcut at chars 4-6 (substring(4,6)); substring(3,5) reads one character early into the token-type field, so the offset is off by one relative to TokenManager.encodeTokenId.

The comment 'Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char' disagrees with the encoding that this PR defines (sessionType chars 1-2, tokenType 3-4, grantType 5-6, e.g. 'trltcc'), and the code reads substring(3,5) — the 4th-5th chars, i.e. the token-type second char plus the grant first char, never the grant shortcut. The comment (and the index) should point at the 5th char / substring(4,6).

issues.descricao: getShortcut() Javadoc says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, but the encoding requires exactly 2-character shortcuts.
issues.textoGolden: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc says getShortcut() returns 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but every implementation introduced in this PR returns a 2-character shortcut ('ac','cc','pg','pc','rt','ro','te','ci','dg') and the encoder relies on exactly 2 chars (encoded context length 6 = 2+2+2). The doc states a length the code does not produce; it should say 2-character shortcut.

Grant shortcuts are registered without enforcing the two-character length required by the decoder. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut, which the new OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation explicitly suggests, produces a seven-character prefix that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects, breaking encode/decode round trips for that grant. Validate shortcut length during registration and dynamic refresh, and document the required two-character format.

The new contract describes getShortcut() as usually returning a three-letter shortcut, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider requires exactly two characters for the grant field (six total prefix characters, decoded with substring(4, 6)). An extension author following this documentation can produce token IDs that the default decoder rejects. Document the required two-character length rather than advertising three letters.

issues.descricao: testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException, so it passes on a NullPointerException from the unset sessionFactory rather than verifying the unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException.
issues.textoGolden: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

comentarios.texto: Catching RuntimeException allows this negative test to pass for an unrelated fixture failure. The fixture constructs the factory without postInit, leaving sessionFactory null; resolving the unregistered `ac` shortcut calls sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream and throws NullPointerException before the decoder's intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException. Catch/assert IllegalArgumentException specifically and provide a factory fixture whose lookup returns no matching grant, so removing the decoder's validation would fail the test.

issues.descricao: Client-credentials (and UMA permission) token issuance never sets the GRANT_TYPE attribute, so their access token ids are encoded with the unknown grant 'na' instead of their shortcut.

comentarios.texto: The new grant metadata falls back to 'na' for client-credentials and UMA tokens because their issuance paths never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on their fresh ClientSessionContext. ClientCredentialsGrantType calls responseBuilder.generateAccessToken directly, and PermissionGrantType delegates to AuthorizationTokenService, so neither executes the new assignment in createTokenResponse; tokens from these known grants therefore carry unknown grant context. Set the grant attribute in both issuance paths before generating the access token.

issues.descricao: Lazy registration of newly deployed grants does not check shortcut uniqueness, so a grant reusing an existing shortcut silently overwrites the reverse mapping and older tokens decode to the wrong grant.

comentarios.texto: Enforce shortcut uniqueness during lazy registration rather than overwriting grantsByShortcuts. If a newly deployed grant B uses existing grant A's shortcut, this path replaces shortcut→A with shortcut→B while retaining both forward entries. Previously issued A tokens then decode as B. Concurrent registrations of two new grants with the same shortcut likewise both succeed, with the last inverse-map write winning. Use collision-aware atomic registration and reject the conflicting grant before publishing its forward mapping.

issues.descricao: getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default, breaking existing custom grant type factories (compile error or AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it).

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: TopicUser.find_by can return nil and then tu.notification_level is dereferenced without a guard. WHY: Causes NoMethodError 500 for users with no TopicUser row for the topic (also crashes if notification_level is nil since nil > Integer raises). HOW: Handle nil e.g. initialize via TopicUser.get/change or create the row before downgrading.

WHAT: GET topics#unsubscribe performs a state-changing mutation (downgrades TopicUser.notification_level and save!) with no CSRF protection. WHY: Allows cross-site/preview-prefetch triggered unsubscribes since GETs are not CSRF-guarded and email scanners/link prefetchers will fire the URL.

WHAT: Topic#unsubscribe_url returns a relative path interpolated into email markdown via user_notifications.rb unsubscribe_url. WHY: Email clients cannot resolve a relative href so the per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails is broken.

WHAT: Shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but other senders using add_unsubscribe_link do not supply it. WHY: Raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or renders a broken link for every other email type that uses the unsubscribe footer.

WHAT: New topicUnsubscribe route at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe collides with existing topic.fromParamsNear /:nearPost route which matches any string including 'unsubscribe'. WHY: Navigation to the unsubscribe URL can resolve to the topic post-stream route with nearPost='unsubscribe' instead of the unsubscribe template, loading the wrong page and feeding a non-numeric nearPost into closestPostForPostNumber/refresh logic. HOW: Define the unsubscribe route before the topic resource, constrain :nearPost to numeric/last, or use a distinct path that cannot match :nearPost.

issues.descricao: The new unsubscribe endpoint changes the user's topic notification level on a plain GET request, so a third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user without any CSRF token.

comentarios.texto: The unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification_level (tu.save!) via a plain GET route (config/routes.rb:440-441) with skip_before_filter :check_xhr, authenticating only through the session cookie. There is no CSRF token (Rails forgery protection does not cover GET) and no capability token, unlike EmailController#unsubscribe which authorizes via DigestUnsubscribeKey. Any third-party page can embed and, when a logged-in user loads it, silently change that user's notification_level for the topic. Require a per-user capability token (like the digest unsubscribe key) in the URL, or perform the state change from an authenticated non-GET request that carries the CSRF token.

The new GET routes mutate the authenticated user's notification preferences without CSRF verification. An attacker can navigate a logged-in user's browser to a known topic unsubscribe URL and reduce or mute its notifications, because Rails excludes GET from forgery-token checks and unsubscribe explicitly skips check_xhr. Make GET render a confirmation page and perform the preference change through a CSRF-protected POST or PUT.

WHAT: The unsubscribe state change (lowering/muting notification_level + save!) runs on a GET route (config/routes.rb GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). WHY: An attacker can forge the URL as an image/prefetch/link to silently change a victim's notification state with no CSRF token since GETs are not CSRF-protected. HOW: Make the mutation a PUT/POST with CSRF protection or require an explicit confirmation parameter/token instead of mutating on page view.

issues.descricao: TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences TopicUser.find_by without handling a missing row, so users with no topic_users record get a NoMethodError/500 instead of being unsubscribed.
issues.textoGolden: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash

comentarios.texto: tu is not checked for nil before use. TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) returns nil whenever the logged-in user has no topic_users row for that topic (the same lookup TopicUser.get performs), and the next line dereferences tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Because the route is only gated by ensure_logged_in, any logged-in user can hit /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe(.json) for a topic they never opened and trigger the crash. Guard the lookup, e.g. `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...); return render json: {success: false} unless tu` (or build/return early) before reading notification_level.

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil (e.g. the user clicks the emailed unsubscribe link for a topic for which no TopicUser row was ever created), and the very next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then `tu.save!`). This raises NoMethodError on nil and the unsubscribe request 500s. Guard the nil case (e.g. return early or use `TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create_by`) before reading/writing notification_level.

`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (find_by yields nil when no row exists), but the next lines dereference it unconditionally (`tu.notification_level`, `tu.save!`). Since the new unsubscribe routes are public GET endpoints, any logged-in user visiting /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never tracked will trigger a NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a sane response. Guard the nil case (e.g. create/skip or redirect) before reading notification_level.

issues.descricao: The message builder spec passes unsubscribe_url in the fixture but never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the email.

comentarios.texto: The `unsubscribe_url` added to the `message_with_unsubscribe` fixture is never asserted. The two tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header `be_present` and that the body matches `user_preferences_url`; neither references `unsubscribe_url`. So they would still pass if the topic-specific unsubscribe URL this PR introduces were dropped or wired to the wrong value. Add an assertion (e.g. that `message_with_unsubscribe.body` matches `/t/1234/unsubscribe`, and that the List-Unsubscribe header points at the topic unsubscribe URL) so the new behaviour is actually covered.

The fixture now passes unsubscribe_url, but no assertion reads it. The tests only check that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains user_preferences_url, so they pass if the topic unsubscribe link is removed or broken. Add an assertion that the body includes "/t/1234/unsubscribe".

issues.descricao: The unsubscribe confirmation says the user will stop receiving notifications for the topic, but watching/tracking users are only moved to regular, which still sends mention/reply notifications.

comentarios.texto: The confirmation promises that the user will stop receiving notifications for this topic, but TopicsController#unsubscribe sets watching/tracking users to regular, not muted. Regular still allows mention/reply notifications, so this confirmation (and the corresponding promise in the new email link text) overstates what clicking the link accomplished. Describe stopping notifications for every new post, or make the confirmation conditional on the resulting notification level so only muted users are told that all topic notifications have stopped.

issues.descricao: Unsubscribe saves the new notification level without setting notifications_reason_id, so auto-tracked topics are promoted back to tracking on the next read, undoing the unsubscribe.

comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

issues.descricao: The topic unsubscribe GET endpoint is not idempotent: each visit steps the notification level down again, so reloading the link moves a topic from regular to muted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Changed SADD/SSCAN to ZADD/ZSCAN with no migration breaks existing Redis keys of Set type. WHY: Redis raises WRONGTYPE when ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN/ZUNIONSTORE hits a pre-deploy Set key (TTL up to 3600s), failing process_spans/flush during rollout. HOW: Handle WRONGTYPE/migrate (e.g., DEL or convert old sets) or version the key.

WHAT: Direct val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError when the field is absent. WHY: One old/malformed SpanEvent crashes the whole process_batch batch instead of skipping/defaulting. HOW: Use val.get("end_timestamp_precise") with a fallback (e.g., now/timestamp) or validate and drop the span.

WHAT: ZUNIONSTORE uses default AGGREGATE SUM so a duplicate payload member gets score+score. WHY: Retried/reprocessed spans double their end_timestamp (~3.4e9), corrupting order so duplicates become unevictable and wrong spans are evicted via ZPOPMIN. HOW: Add "AGGREGATE", "MAX" to both ZUNIONSTORE calls.

WHAT: Redirect-chase limit cut from 10000 to 1000 with no functional need. WHY: Segment trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 stop resolving early and spans are joined into the wrong set, silently splitting/corrupting segments. HOW: Restore 10000 limit or keep eviction cap (1000 spans) separate from traversal depth.

WHAT: ZPOPMIN eviction by lowest end_timestamp can evict the segment/root span payload while hrs flag stays "1". WHY: Downstream flush then emits a segment marked has-root without the root span, producing a corrupt segment. HOW: Protect the segment span from eviction or clear/adjust hrs handling when it is evicted.

WHAT: Flush path removed the max_segment_spans span-count guard, leaving max_segment_spans config dead. WHY: Any segment bypassing Lua eviction (legacy sets, races, future callers) is now flushed unbounded instead of skipped, breaking downstream size assumptions. HOW: Re-add a span-count check after ZSCAN pagination or explicitly wire max_segment_spans to the Lua cap.

issues.descricao: ZUNIONSTORE merges sorted sets with the default SUM aggregate, so a span payload present in both keys gets a doubled end-timestamp score and is wrongly kept by the oldest-first eviction.

comentarios.texto: ZUNIONSTORE uses AGGREGATE SUM by default, so when the same span payload is present in both `set_key` and the merged `span_key`/`parent_key` (duplicate delivery is anticipated by this buffer's own comments), its score is added instead of being kept equal to `end_timestamp_precise`. Because eviction at line 63 (`zpopmin` by score) compares scores across all members of `set_key`, a summed score makes the duplicated span appear far newer than its real end timestamp and biases eviction away from legitimately-old spans, breaking the stated 'evict oldest end timestamps' contract. Use ZUNIONSTORE ... AGGREGATE MIN (or MAX) so a duplicate keeps a single end timestamp score rather than doubling it.

ZUNIONSTORE uses its default SUM aggregation, so replayed payloads present in both the temporary parent_key and the resolved set_key receive the sum of their end timestamps. Replaying a child whose parent already redirects to an ancestor therefore makes that old span score roughly twice its actual timestamp, protecting it from eviction over genuinely newer spans. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN for identical timestamp scores) on both union operations to preserve timestamp scores when members overlap.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, so a payload present in both the destination and source has its timestamp doubled rather than preserved. This can happen when a previously merged span is replayed into its original subtree key. The duplicated span then sorts after genuinely newer spans and survives ZPOPMIN eviction incorrectly. Specify AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN, since identical payloads should have identical timestamps) on both union calls so merging remains idempotent and scores remain end timestamps.

issues.descricao: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under the same key names, so keys left by the previous release make ZADD, ZCARD and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, crashing span processing and flushing.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Changed SET ops (scard/sunionstore) to ZSET ops (zcard/zunionstore/zpopmin) with no migration breaks in-flight segments. WHY: Old keys of type SET still live up to TTL; ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZADD on the opposite type raises WRONGTYPE and fails inserts/flushes during rollout.

The segment keys were migrated from Redis SETs to SORTED SETs (ZADD/ZSCAN/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN), but nothing handles the keys written by the currently deployed release. During a rolling deploy, an existing `span-buf:s:{...}:{id}` key is still a SET, so this `p.zadd(...)` (and the flusher's `p.zscan(...)`, and the Lua `zcard`/`zunionstore`) raises WRONGTYPE 'Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value'. That exception is unhandled: it aborts the whole pipeline/Lua invocation and crashes the consumer batch. Add a key-schema version to the key name (or a migration/fallback) so old SET-typed keys cannot be touched as sorted sets.

The new ZADD writes sorted sets into the same span-buf:s namespace previously populated by SADD, without migrating existing set keys. During deployment, inserting into an existing buffered segment fails with WRONGTYPE, and the new ZSCAN reader likewise fails on pending old-format segments instead of flushing them. Introduce a coordinated migration/drain or a versioned namespace with compatible handling of pending old-format buffers.

issues.descricao: Claims zpopmin eviction can drop the root span while the has-root flag stays set, flushing a segment without its root.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zpopmin eviction by lowest end_timestamp has no protection for the segment/root span. WHY: Root with smallest or tied timestamp (tests use identical timestamps, ties break lexicographically) is evicted while hrs flag stays 1, flushing a root-marked segment missing its root.

issues.descricao: max_segment_spans is still a constructor parameter but is no longer enforced; the segment cap is now hardcoded to 1000 in the Lua script, so the configured value is ignored.

comentarios.texto: This hunk removes the only load-time span-count cap (`self.max_segment_spans`): previously a segment exceeding 1001 spans was logged, deleted from `payloads`/`cursors`, and skipped, but now every scanned span is unconditionally appended via `payloads[key].extend(...)`. The new bound relies entirely on insert-time eviction in the Lua script; if that eviction fails to bound a key (e.g. duplicated/scored members or the concurrent-writer case the code itself warns about at lines 457-461), this method will now materialize an unbounded number of spans into memory and emit them, whereas before it was safely skipped. Re-introduce a span-count guard (or verify the invite-time eviction strictly caps cardinality) to keep memory bounded.

buffer.py declares the segment span limit as the configurable `max_segment_spans` (default 1001, line 150) and this hunk removed the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` size guard from the flush path, while the other changed file (add-buffer.lua line 62) now enforces a hardcoded cap of 1000 spans. The two changed files disagree on what the segment span limit is: the Lua cap (1000) is not the declared `max_segment_spans`, and the buffer no longer applies the declared limit at all. If `max_segment_spans` is configured below 1000 (or below the Lua cap), oversized segments that this code used to skip will now be flushed. Reconcile the constant: either keep/restore the buffer-side guard against `self.max_segment_spans`, or make the Lua cap derive from the same limit instead of hardcoding 1000.

The segment size cap is hardcoded as 1000 here, but SpansBuffer still declares max_segment_spans = 1001 in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py, and this PR deleted the flush-time guard that used that constant. The declared limit and the actually-enforced limit now disagree (and the Python constant is no longer honored anywhere). Make the Lua cap and the Python constant agree — either pass max_segment_spans in as an ARGV instead of the literal 1000, or update the declared constant to 1000 — so the buffer's enforced bound matches the value it declares.

issues.descricao: Tests give every span the same end timestamp and never exceed 1000 spans, so the new score ordering and oldest-first eviction are not tested.

comentarios.texto: All spans in the fixture use identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0, so the ZSET score-dependent behavior (ordering by end time, zunionstore score merge, and Lua zpopmin keeping newest 1000) is neutralised — tests pass even if scores are wrong or eviction keeps the wrong end. Use distinct timestamps and add a >1000-span trimming test asserting oldest evicted.
The missing test for the new trim path (zset ordering/trim by end_timestamp_precise, the >1000-span zpopmin path) is a coverage gap. Add a test that verifies the new trim behavior.

issues.descricao: The span redirect-walk limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 iterations, so trees deeper than 1000 may not resolve to the correct segment root.
The spans buffer module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as plain sets, though they are now sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise and trimmed to 1000 spans by add-buffer.lua.
The set_key variable name no longer matches the sorted-set data type after the switch to zadd/zscan.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: New getCredentials() dereferences myUser without a null check (myUser.recoveryCodes). WHY: Throws NPE for unknown/removed users during federated credential lookup, crashing authentication where sibling methods (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) explicitly null-guard. HOW: Return Stream.empty() when getMyUser(user) is null before touching fields.

WHAT: Changed lookup now returns federated recovery credentials via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, but exhaustion cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById which only deletes from the local store. WHY: An exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is never removed (local delete misses the federated id), leaving stale all-used credentials and forcing repeated re-configuration instead of clean rotation.

WHAT: Federated recovery codes are stored as raw JSON via updateCredential with no consumption/invalidation wiring, unlike the local path where RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid removes the used code and calls updateStoredCredential. WHY: A federated validator that only checks equality (as the PR reference impl does with anyMatch) re-accepts an already-used recovery code indefinitely, allowing replay of single-use backup codes.

issues.descricao: The test user-storage provider validates recovery codes without consuming the used code, so the same code can be replayed.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new recovery-codes branch of isValid only checks whether the submitted code appears in the stored list and never removes the consumed entry. WHY: Unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (which calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode()+updateStoredCredential), the federated path never consumes a code and allCodesUsed() can never become true, so a used recovery code remains valid and can be replayed indefinitely. HOW: On a successful match, remove that entry from the stored codes (rewrite recoveryCodes.credentialData), mirroring the local provider's consume-on-success semantics.

The new recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list without consuming the accepted code. Repeating a successful login with the same code succeeds indefinitely, while getCredentials reconstructs all original codes so the login form never advances or detects exhaustion. Validate the next unused code and persist its consumption before returning success.

The new federated recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list but never removes a successfully used code from myUser.recoveryCodes. Consequently the same recovery code remains valid on subsequent logins, and getCredentials reconstructs the full original set every time. Consume and persist the successfully validated code (and test a second login/replay), so federated recovery codes retain their one-time semantics.

issues.descricao: getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-codes credential without copying the stored credential id, so the returned federated credential has a null id and cannot be targeted by id-based removal.
issues.textoGolden: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getCredentials builds the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues but never sets its id from the stored myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (createFromValues does not populate id). WHY: The returned federated model has a null id, so callers that identify/delete the credential by id — e.g. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) when all codes are used, or federated-credential deletion via getFederatedCredentialsStream — cannot target the actual credential. HOW: call model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()) after createFromValues.

getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-code model without copying the ID assigned during updateCredential. createFromValues does not assign an ID, so the exposed federated credential has a null ID and CredentialDeleteHelper cannot resolve it by the stored credential ID for account deletion. Copy myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() to the reconstructed model before returning it.

The CredentialModel returned from getCredentials for recovery codes is built with createFromValues and never gets the stored credential's id (myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()). RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator later calls removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) once all codes are used, and this would pass a null id. Fix: call model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()) after creating the model.

issues.descricao: Creating recovery codes in external storage does not remove a previously stored local recovery-codes credential, and validation falls back to local storage, so the replaced codes still authenticate.

comentarios.texto: Successful recovery-code creation in external storage leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential active. For a federated user who previously stored codes locally and now has an external provider supporting this type, regeneration no longer calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential's replacement cleanup; UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to the local validator when external validation rejects an old code, so the supposedly replaced codes still authenticate. Remove the previous local recovery-code credential after successful external creation.

issues.descricao: Exhausted recovery codes are removed with removeStoredCredentialById, which only covers local storage, so a federated recovery-codes credential is never removed.

comentarios.texto: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() can now return a credential from user storage (federated), but this code still calls removeStoredCredentialById() on it once all codes are used. That removal only targets local stored credentials, so a federated credential may not be removed. The user could then be left with an exhausted credential in user storage. Remove federated credentials through the federated path, or confirm the removal reaches user storage.

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a credential from user storage, but exhausted codes are cleaned up with removeStoredCredentialById, which only targets the local DB. For a federated credential (possibly with a null id), the exhausted credential is never removed or the call misbehaves, so the user keeps a dead credential. Remove federated credentials through a path that covers user storage, for example by checking where the credential came from.

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated credential. The authenticator still removes an exhausted one with removeStoredCredentialById(getId()), which only deletes from the local store, and the federated model's id may be null. Remove the credential through the path that matches where it was found, for example by checking whether it came from the federated stream and using the federated removal.

issues.descricao: Looking up recovery codes now always queries the federated provider first, which for LDAP users adds an LDAP round-trip and can throw IllegalStateException, failing recovery-code login with a 500.
An error log in the test user storage hard-codes the credential type as 'recovery-codes' instead of using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE ('recovery-authn-codes').

The test federation provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage regenerates the recovery-codes model from the raw list on every getCredentials and never records consumed codes, so the next-code number and allCodesUsed() never reflect usage for its users.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? does case-sensitive exact lookup BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. WHY: Attacker bypasses block by changing case (e.g. FOO@bar.com vs foo@bar.com) while domain checks use case-insensitive Regexp and codebase normalizes via Email.downcase elsewhere. HOW: Normalize both sides with Email.downcase(email).strip before query (and on create).

WHAT: validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block? which mutates DB (match_count+=1, last_match_at, save) inside validation. WHY: Rails runs validations twice per create (valid? + save) so one signup attempt inflates match_count by 2 and updates last_match_at spuriously, corrupting blocked-stats. HOW: Make validation side-effect-free and increment stats once in controller/service after failed save, or guard with atomic update_counters outside validator.

WHAT: emailValidation depends on 'rejectedEmails.@each' for an array of primitive strings. WHY: @each observes properties of array items, not membership; pushObject(result.values.email) does not invalidate the computed property so the remembered rejected email error is not shown until accountEmail itself changes. HOW: Change dependent key to 'rejectedEmails.[]' (or 'rejectedEmails.length').

WHAT: EmailValidator.validate_each only checks whitelist/blacklist/blocked and never validates email syntax, while User now relies solely on validates :email, email:true for email shape. WHY: Malformed strings with no @/domain pass validation and create users with undeliverable emails, breaking mail delivery and downstream assumptions. HOW: Restore a format check (e.g. against User::EMAIL) in EmailValidator before the restriction/blocked checks.

issues.descricao: When the server rejects an email, the signup form marks it with the generic 'invalid email' text instead of the server's reason (blocked or not allowed).

comentarios.texto: The message shown for a rejected email disagrees with the reason the code is reacting to. This branch fires when the server rejected the email (result.errors.email), and this PR gives that condition its own server string — user.email.blocked, added in config/locales/server.en.yml as "is not allowed." — but the client re-labels it with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). A user whose address is perfectly well-formed but blocked/hosted on a blacklisted domain is therefore told their email is invalid, contradicting the reason just returned by the server. Use the blocked/not-allowed message (and add a matching client locale key) instead of user.email.invalid. Notice the same generic string is used at line ~94 for validation failures, so it should not be reused to represent a distinct server-side rejection.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match and no normalisation, so changing the letter case of a blocked address bypasses the block list.
issues.textoGolden: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

comentarios.texto: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.
Case-sensitivity bypass: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is exact case-sensitive with no normalization, while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and lookup.

issues.descricao: BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count and last_match_at as a side effect of email validation, so each signup attempt (validated twice) inflates the counter and concurrent updates can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: should_block? mutates match_count/last_match_at via read-modify-write save inside a validator. WHY: Every validation call (including re-validations of the same attempt or attempts failing on unrelated fields like username) inflates stats, and concurrent signups lose increments with no atomic update. HOW: Move stats update out of validation or use atomic increment (update_counters/increment_counter) only on actual blocked rejections.

WHAT: `should_block?` mutates state (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, calls `record.save`) inside a method that is invoked from the model validation callback, and the signup controller runs validation twice per attempt (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168 then `user.save` at :172). WHY: a single signup attempt increments `match_count` twice and rewrites `last_match_at`, so the per-email block statistics the feature was built to track are wrong. HOW: make the read side non-mutating for validation and record the match separately (e.g. move the increment out of validation, or guard it so it runs once per attempt), keeping the predicate pure.

WHAT: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock or unique constraint protection. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` and one write overwrites the other, losing counts, so the tracked statistics drift under load. HOW: use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or a database-level counter increment.

issues.descricao: Claims the 'returns false' spec cannot distinguish nil from false because be_false is a truthiness matcher.

comentarios.texto: This test is named "returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist," but it cannot verify that. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]`, which yields `nil` (not `false`) when no record exists, and under this suite's RSpec 2 semantics `subject.should be_false` is a truthiness matcher that passes for any falsy value including `nil`. The assertion therefore passes on the nil the code actually returns and would only fail on an outright `true`; it does not pin the `false`/`nil` distinction its name asserts. Assert the value exactly (e.g. `subject.should == false`, or `be_falsey`/`be_nil` if nil is intended) so a regression returning a non-false falsy value is caught.

issues.descricao: The domain whitelist/blacklist regex @(domains) is not anchored at the end, so an address like user@example.com.evil.com matches a whitelist entry for example.com and bypasses the restriction.
issues.textoGolden: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: email_in_restriction_setting? builds unanchored Regexp "@(domains)" with only '.' escaped. WHY: Whitelist 'gmail.com' substring-matches 'victim@gmail.com.evil.com', so an attacker registers with an unapproved domain and bypasses the allow-list; blacklist similarly over/under-matches and other regex metachars are unescaped. HOW: Anchor and escape domains (e.g. Regexp.escape per domain split on '|' plus /\A[^@\s]+@(?:domain)\z/i).

issues.descricao: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.
A spec comment says last_match_at shows whether an email has ever been blocked, but should_block? updates it on every match, including do_nothing records.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the delegate is gone, violating GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() contract documented as Never returns null. WHY: callers expecting non-null Long can NPE on unboxing or misbehave (count shown as unknown vs 0), turning a fixed NPE into a downstream null-dereference. HOW: return a non-null sentinel (e.g. 0L) or throw/handle deleted-group at caller instead of leaking null.

WHAT: reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() and never joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. WHY: assertion races with an in-flight request and the leaked thread keeps hitting the server after the test, so failures after the assert are missed and later tests are polluted — flaky/false-passing test. HOW: keep the Thread reference, join it (with timeout) after deletedAll.set(true) before asserting.

WHAT: reader thread tight-loops groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) with no sleep/backoff while deletes run. WHY: each iteration requests unbounded full top-level group list, hammering server/DB in a hot spin and slowing the suite. HOW: page with a bounded maxResults and add a small sleep/yield or iteration cap.

issues.descricao: The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: BuildIndex no longer serializes whole builds — only the final cache write at b.cache[key]=idx is locked, so concurrent builds for the same key run fully in parallel. WHY: Two goroutines building the same NamespacedResource both call bleve.New on the same dir (filepath.Join(Root,Namespace,Resource.Group)) and both run ListIterator+Write+Flush, causing duplicate work, file-handle/dir contention and last-wins cache clobbering with double IndexTenants.Inc. HOW: Restore per-key mutual exclusion (singleflight or per-key lock) around the build, keeping the fine-grained cache lock only for the map write.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) but on error returns nil,err without invoking s.cancel (or Stop), leaking the cancellable watcher context and any partially started lifecycle/search watch resources. WHY: Failed construction leaves the context.Background-derived s.ctx and its goroutines (broadcaster/search watch) uncancelled with no handle to clean up, leaking resources on every failed startup/index-build attempt. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (or defer cleanup) before returning nil,err.

issues.descricao: BuildIndex now locks only the final cache assignment, so concurrent callers for the same uncached key all build the same expensive index in parallel and the last one overwrites the others.
issues.textoGolden: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Removing the function-wide `b.cacheMu.Lock()/defer Unlock()` and keeping only the lock around `b.cache[key]=idx` removes the only thing that serialized GetIndex against an in-flight build. WHY: getOrCreateIndex (resource/search.go:287-307) does GetIndex -> if nil -> build; previously BuildIndex held the write lock for its whole body so a concurrent caller's GetIndex (RLock) blocked until the first build cached the index and then saw it (no second build). Now GetIndex can return nil while a build for the same key is still running, so two requests/watch events build the SAME key concurrently — producing two distinct index instances where the caller holding the non-cached one never observes later writes (stale search results), and, for file-backed indices (size > FileThreshold), two concurrent `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` opening the same on-disk directory. HOW: guard the build per key (e.g. re-check the cache under the write lock after acquiring it, or use a per-key single-flight/lock so only one build runs per NamespacedResource), rather than relying on a global write lock held for the entire body.

The cache mutex was moved to cover only the cache assignment, removing the serialization that previously surrounded the whole BuildIndex. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can now both construct an index (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same on-disk path) and both write `b.cache[key]`; the second overwrites the first, so callers get distinct index instances for one key and writes made through the losing instance are invisible to readers of the cached one (and the file-backed build may collide on the same directory). Keep the build for a given key serialized (e.g. restore the lock around the build, or take a per-key lock) instead of locking only the map write.

Locking only cache publication allows concurrent requests for the same uncached key to build separate indexes and overwrite each other's cache entries. Search and handleEvent both call getOrCreateIndex, whose GetIndex previously blocked behind the build-wide lock; now an event can update one newly built index before another build replaces it, losing that update from subsequent search results and leaving the discarded index open. Serialize builds per NamespacedResource and recheck the cache after acquiring that per-key guard.

issues.descricao: The new startup log calls TotalDocs, which iterates the index cache without a lock, after the event goroutine that can add indexes has started, so a concurrent map read and write can crash the process.
issues.textoGolden: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

comentarios.texto: The newly added `s.search.TotalDocs()` call is unsafe: `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-150) iterates `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`, while the bleve.go hunk in this same PR keeps `cacheMu` for the `b.cache[key] = idx` write only. Because search.go:207-213 already started the watch-event goroutine that can call `build` → `BuildIndex` → cache write, line 216 can iterate the map concurrently with that write, causing a `concurrent map iteration and map write` panic or data race. Either guard the `TotalDocs` read with `cacheMu`, or move this call to a point where no build can run concurrently.

The new startup log calls TotalDocs after launching the write-event listener, but bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without cacheMu.RLock. A write event for an unindexed resource can concurrently publish an index through BuildIndex, causing a map iteration/write race and potentially a fatal runtime error during initialization. Protect TotalDocs cache iteration with the same read lock used by GetIndex.

BuildIndex now writes b.cache under Lock while TotalDocs (called from search.init after the watch goroutine starts) ranges over b.cache without any lock. This can cause a concurrent map read/write fatal error. Fix by taking cacheMu.RLock in TotalDocs.

issues.descricao: NewResourceServer returns an error when Init fails without cancelling the server context created earlier.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) and, on error, returns `nil, err` without invoking the `cancel` func created at line 229 and without running any lifecycle cleanup. WHY: Init may have already started long-lived goroutines — searchSupport.init's event-consumption loop uses context.Background() (resource/search.go:202) and initWatcher starts a watcher bound to s.ctx (server.go:752-770) — so if search.init succeeds and initWatcher (or a later step) fails, the constructor discards the server while those goroutines keep running with no way to stop them, leaking the internal context and watcher goroutines. HOW: on the error path call `cancel()` (and any needed lifecycle.Stop) before returning, or defer the cancel until success.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously but returns nil,err without calling the cancel created for s.ctx. WHY: Failed startup leaks the server context (and any lifecycle/watch resources partially started by Init), leaving goroutines/channel watches alive. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (and lifecycle Stop cleanup) before returning.

issues.descricao: The PR skips the storage-server module integration test on postgres instead of fixing the failure, removing coverage of the new eager initialization on postgres.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym without nil guard, crashing when default_locale is nil/unloaded. WHY: The PR description itself states default_locale is not guaranteed loaded at boot, so the first fallback resolution raises NoMethodError on nil instead of falling back to :en. HOW: Use SiteSetting.default_locale.try(:to_sym) / safe navigation so compact can drop nil.

WHAT: ensure_loaded! is only wired in the web-request set_locale path, while fallbacks affect every translate (PostAlerter I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale), Jobs::Base I18n.locale= path). WHY: Background/mailers resolve fallback chains to locales never loaded, returning missing translations despite the fallback feature. HOW: Call FallbackLocaleList ensure/preload in those non-request paths or make load_locale lazy-safe for fallback locales.

WHAT: New I18n.ensure_loaded! forwards attacker-influenced locale (User#effective_locale -> self.locale, unchecked) into load_locale which builds Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$") without escaping. WHY: A locale containing regex metacharacters (e.g. ".*") changes which load_path entries match and get loaded, enabling load amplification / ReDoS via crafted profile locale. HOW: Escape with Regexp.escape(locale.to_s) and validate locale against LocaleSiteSetting.supported_locales before loading.

WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] performs a SiteSetting.default_locale lookup on every fallback resolution. WHY: With fallbacks enabled the backend consults fallbacks[locale] per translate/miss, turning hundreds of per-request translates into hundreds of settings lookups and slowing the hot translation path. HOW: Memoize/cache default_locale per request or compute fallback chain once per locale change instead of per key.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Queries interpolated with applyTemplateVariables at line 299 are interpolated again downstream (DataSourceWithBackend.query re-applies applyTemplateVariables before backend, and shard path calls runSplitQuery after already interpolating). WHY: applyTemplateVariables calls addAdHocFilters, so the second/third pass re-adds the same adhocFilters to an expr that already contains them, producing duplicated labels/wrong expr. HOW: Interpolate once at the entry point and strip filters/scopedVars from sub-requests, or make downstream passes skip applyTemplateVariables/adHoc when already applied.

WHAT: New code filters empty expr before interpolation, while old code interpolated via interpolateVariablesInQueries first then filtered. WHY: A query with truthy raw expr (e.g. "$var") that interpolates to empty/falsey is now kept and sent to splitQueriesByStreamShard/shard fetching instead of being dropped, causing empty-selector fetch and invalid sub-queries. HOW: Move the .filter(query.expr) to after the .map(applyTemplateVariables) or filter on the interpolated expr.

issues.descricao: Loki split/shard queries are now interpolated with applyTemplateVariables before splitting and again on execution, so ad hoc filters are applied twice and already-substituted values are re-interpolated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 52), but it then delegates each sub-request to runSplitQuery (line 163), which this PR also changed to call datasource.applyTemplateVariables again (querySplitting.ts:299), so each target is interpolated (and ad hoc filters applied) twice. WHY: double interpolation re-runs addAdHocFilters on an already-filtered expression; the stream-selector path masks the duplicate via labelExists() dedup in addFilterToStreamSelector (modifyQuery.ts:494), but parsed/structured-metadata labels use addFilterAsLabelFilter which does not dedup, producing duplicated label filters, and any interpolated value containing '$' can be re-interpolated. This is confirmed by the updated test expecting applyTemplateVariables toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) for a single target (1 call here + 4 sub-requests through runSplitQuery) instead of 1. HOW: interpolate only once — either remove the interpolation added to runShardSplitQuery and let runSplitQuery do it, or have splitQueriesByStreamShard pass the already-interpolated targets without re-interpolating in runSplitQuery.

The newly interpolated targets are interpolated again by DataSourceWithBackend.query when runQuery executes each split request. TemplateSrv.replace scans the resulting string again, so a variable whose literal value contains another defined variable token (for example, a log-search value containing `$other`) is expanded a second time and produces a different query from the non-splitting path; shard splitting also passes through this additional interpolation. Preserve the early interpolation needed for partitioning while ensuring already-interpolated targets are not interpolated again on execution, and test through the real backend query preparation rather than mocking runQuery.

Targets are interpolated here with `applyTemplateVariables`, including ad hoc filters, and then sent to `datasource.runQuery`, which interpolates them again through the backend path (datasource.ts:324/377). The ad hoc filters may be injected twice, and already-substituted values are re-interpolated, which can produce wrong or invalid LogQL. Interpolate only once. Either clear `scopedVars` and `filters` on the sub-requests after the first pass, or skip interpolation in `runQuery` for already-interpolated requests. The same issue applies to shardQuerySplitting.ts:52.

issues.descricao: runShardSplitQuery now filters empty/hidden targets before interpolation, so an expr that interpolates to an empty string is no longer dropped.

comentarios.texto: The order of operations was inverted relative to the previous contract: interpolation used to run before the `expr`/`hide` filters (interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets).filter(...)), and now the filters run on the *raw* targets before `applyTemplateVariables` is applied. Filtering on the un-interpolated `query.expr` means the previous fallback that dropped a target once variable substitution had emptied its expression no longer exists: a target like `{ expr: '$myVar' }` whose variable resolves to '' is truthy at filter time, survives, is then interpolated to `''`, and is passed into the shard splitting/execution loop as a blank query. To preserve the old contract the filters should run on the interpolated result (or the interpolated expr should be re-checked for emptiness).

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware reuses a single shared *MetricsMiddleware and mutates imw.next on every CreateClientMiddleware call. WHY: Decorator.clientFromMiddlewares rebuilds the chain per request, so concurrent requests concurrently write/read imw.next causing a data race and potentially routing through another request's downstream chain. HOW: Allocate a new MetricsMiddleware per call (copy pluginMetrics/registry, set next) like ContextualLoggerMiddleware/LoggerMiddleware do.

WHAT: logRequest dropped explicit pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname/traceID fields and now relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). WHY: Those fields only appear if upstream NewContextualLoggerMiddleware ran and global contextual/trace providers are registered, so standalone use or reordering of LoggerMiddleware silently loses plugin/request identity in logs. HOW: Keep explicit fields or document/enforce the ordering dependency.

WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns a fresh NewTestLogger(). WHY: Calls like m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info in LoggerMiddleware record on a throwaway logger, so assertions on the injected fake see zero calls and context/state is lost unlike the real wrapper which derives from the receiver. HOW: Return the receiver (or a derived copy sharing its capture) instead of a new instance.

issues.descricao: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so logs written via the contextual logger are lost to assertions on the original fake.
issues.textoGolden: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger instead of the receiver. WHY: LoggerMiddleware calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info so the write goes to a throwaway instance and assertions on the original TestLogger Calls/Message never observe it, diverging from real wrapper that preserves logger context. HOW: Return f (or a child sharing f) instead of NewTestLogger.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a throwaway LoginFormsProvider from context.form() that is never rendered. WHY: context.form() creates a new provider per call (AuthenticationProcessor.java:589-612), and both callers render with a different instance — WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse uses at least 3 distinct context.form() calls (setError, setup, fillContextForm, errorChallenge) and badPasswordHandler renders via challenge() with a fresh instance — so after a passkey/password error during re-auth the flags are lost, falling back to editable-username regular login. HOW: Set the attributes on the same provider instance used to render (e.g., return/pass the form or set them after fillContextForm inside the rendering path).

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

issues.descricao: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so the hidden webauthn form is guaranteed by isPasskeysEnabled() and the new per-user isConfiguredFor check for users without a passkey is never exercised in UsernamePasswordForm.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Write lock is acquired at line 48 without re-checking the cache and is held across blocking file/CDN I/O. WHY: Concurrent cache misses that all passed the RLock check serialize on the exclusive lock and each redoes manifest file/network reads, while concurrent cache-hit readers needing RLock block for the full I/O duration. HOW: Re-check entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock and return early on hit, and only hold the lock for publishing the pointer (do I/O outside the lock or use singleflight).

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets holds a global exclusive mutex through the whole manifest load, so in Dev mode, where the cache is bypassed, every request serializes behind it.
